s.cutWaistband-back.d: The **Waistband** (3) is a rectangular piece of fabric {{{ w }}} wide and {{{ l }}} long.
s.cutElasticLength.d:
You will need about {{{ length }}}, but definitely less than {{{ max }}} of an elastic band for your waistband. The elastic will need to be able to stretch an additional {{ fac }}% of its original length.

(This does not include seam allowance)
s.waistbandAngle.d: Based on our (very rough) estimation, your optimal front waistband angle is {{ angle }}°.
s.waistHipsRatio.d: This pattern assumes that your waist is smaller than your hips. If you have a larger waist than hips, the waistband may slip easily and you may need to do manual changes to the pattern to fit your body.
s.hipsSeatRatio.d: This pattern assumes that your hips are smaller than your seat. If you have a larger hips than seat, the waistband might not fit over your hips and you may need to do manual changes to the pattern to fit your body.
s.badWaistbandHeight.d: We could not fit the waistband to your specifications. Try to increase the waist height option or reduce the width of the waistband elastic.
s.badCrotchDepth.d:
We use the waist-to-upper-leg measurement, the crotch depth measurement and the difference between waist-to-floor and inseam measurements (if given) to estimate a minimum depth of the crotch seam. Based on your measurements, our estimations for the correct crotch depth vary significantly, ranging from {{ min }} to {{ max }} with {{ cur }} as the assumed correct value.

You may wish to verify your measurements.
s.badCrotchDepth2.d:
Our estimated crotch depth of {{ cd }} was smaller than your waist-to-seat measurement of {{ ws }}.

Please measure the seat around the widest part of your bum, even if your body is wider below that. The waist-to-upper-leg measurement and the crotch depth measurement must physically both be larger than waist-to-seat.
s.legCircumference.d: The leg holes in this pattern have a circumference of {{ circ }}, which is {{ pct }} more than your upper leg circumference measurement of {{ measurement }}.
s.waistbandAngleNotes: This calculation assumes that your body has a constant slope between the waist and hips. Most bodies don't work that way, so take this suggestion with a grain of salt.

elasticHeight.d: Height of the elastic used in the waistband

legBalance.d: Balance between front and back leg width

inseam.d: Length of the inseam from crotch to hem

crotchLower.d: Lower the crotch depth for a more relaxed fit

ease.d: Amount of ease added to the waist and hips

waistReduction.d: Reduction of the ease around the waist

crossSeamEase.d: Amount of ease added to the cross seam for comfort

waistHeight.d: Height of the waistband relative to natural waist

fitLegs.d: Adjust the fit of the legs from loose to tight

splitParts.d: Split the front and back parts into separate pattern pieces

splitPartsYes.d: Front and back are separate pattern pieces

splitPartsNo.d: Front and back are combined in one pattern piece

sideSplit.d: Create a slit on the side

sideSplitYes.d: Add a slit on the side

sideSplitNo.d: Use a full height side seam

sideSplitOffset.d: Determines the height at which the split starts

pocket.d: Which type of front pockets you want

pocket.patch.d: Add patch pockets at the front

pocket.inset.d: Add inset pockets at the front

waistbandFrontAngle.d: How curved the waistband is at the front

elasticOnlyOnBack.d: Keep the front free of elastic, only use elastic on the back

waistbandExtraWidth.d: Make the waistband tunnel a bit wider than the elastic for easier sewing
